key_insight: NeoGx uses early NICU electronic health record data to predict which neonates are likely to need genetic evaluation within 18 months, helping direct rapid genome sequencing to the infants most likely to benefit.
clinical_relevance: If used in Level IV NICUs, the tool could accelerate genetic workup and shorten time to diagnosis for critically ill newborns.
method: 14,272 Level IV NICU patients were split into development, calibration, and independent validation cohorts.
The model used structured EHR data plus phenotypes extracted from clinical text.
Performance was tested after accumulating predictions over the first four NICU weeks.
evidence_signal: In independent validation, NeoGx achieved ROC AUC 0.849 and PR AUC 0.771, and referral guided by the model reduced mean time to first genetic evaluation from 44 to 29 days.
watch_item: Results come from a single-system retrospective EHR study, so external validation and workflow testing are needed before broad implementation.
paper_title: NeoGx: Machine-Recommended Rapid Genome Sequencing for Neonates
